about: Scenes for the animated video of Your First AI Product Team. Each scene starts at a phrase in the narration ("at"); keys ending in At name phrases that trigger a move inside the scene. Chapter cards are added by render.mjs. The scores are from the article's figure.

scenes.at: Most teams start their AI journey
scenes.label: The common first step
scenes.text: One general-purpose assistant, asked to do everything.

scenes.at: The result is usually inconsistent quality
scenes.label: The trap
cards: Strong in one area, weak in another.

scenes.at: A better mental model is to design an AI product team
scenes.label: A better mental model
scenes.text: Specialized agents with clear roles, clear inputs, and clear success criteria.

scenes.at: Context overload.
scenes.label: Why one chatbot fails in real product work
cards: It doesn't know which sources to trust, or which priorities matter today.
Strong in one area and weak in another, and nobody knows why.
When something is wrong, it's unclear which part failed and how to fix it.

scenes.at: Each agent has a role description
scenes.label: Design each agent like a role on a team

scenes.at: A practical starting squad
scenes.label: A practical starting squad

scenes.at: The biggest mistake is starting with the technology
scenes.label: Step 1
scenes.text: Pick a recurring ritual that's expensive in time and attention: backlog grooming, the insights review, quarterly planning.

scenes.at: Then ask: where do we lose time
scenes.label: Three questions about the workflow

scenes.at: Researcher Agent.
scenes.label: Researcher agent: keep you informed
cards: Call notes and transcripts, support tickets, competitor pages, your documents.
Weekly themes, competitive snapshots, source-linked summaries.
Doesn't make product decisions or invent sources. Flags uncertainty.

scenes.at: Analyst Agent.
scenes.label: Analyst agent: decision-ready insights
cards: Analytics dashboards, event data, cohort metrics, experiment results.
Metric narratives, segment and cohort ideas, anomaly summaries.
No causality without experiments. Observation kept apart from hypothesis.

scenes.at: Copywriter Agent.
scenes.label: Copywriter agent: faster, consistent messaging
cards: The feature, the audience, your style guide, regulated-language rules.
Microcopy options, release notes, FAQs, value propositions.
Doesn't make up capabilities. Avoids risky claims. Flags legal review.
cardAt: does not make up product capabilities

scenes.at: Experiment Designer Agent.
scenes.label: Experiment Designer agent: better tests
cards: The hypothesis, primary and guardrail metrics, traffic, past learnings.
An experiment brief, variants, instrumentation, a launch checklist.
Doesn't pick strategy. Proposes options and tradeoffs.

scenes.at: A squad works when outputs become inputs
scenes.label: The handoff: outputs become inputs
items: surfaces a theme and the evidence
proposes how to test a change

scenes.at: A simple MVP scope
scenes.label: Step 3: the MVP squad, useful every week
cards: Top five pain points with sources, plus a monthly competitor digest.
A KPI narrative for 3 to 5 metrics, plus anomaly alerts.
A one-page brief and a launch checklist.
Three microcopy options per feature, one release note.

scenes.at: Use a lightweight rubric across four factors
scenes.label: Step 4: score each agent on four factors
cards: How often does the workflow happen?
How much PM and team time does it take?
What's the downside if it goes wrong?

scenes.at: The Analyst might score high
scenes.label: Which agent to build first (the article's example)
scenes.note: The highest weekly value, at a risk you can manage.

scenes.at: The squad should fit into the tools
scenes.label: Step 5: plug into the tools you already use

scenes.at: A practical pattern
scenes.label: A practical pattern

scenes.at: Treat each agent like a mini product
scenes.label: Step 6: evaluate each agent like a product
cards: Coverage, traceability, and whether leaders cite it.
Consistent briefs, fewer failed launches, faster cycles.
Fewer edits, clarity, brand voice and compliance.

scenes.at: If you cannot evaluate it, it will drift
scenes.text: If you cannot evaluate it, it will drift.

scenes.at: When you move from a chatbot to a squad
scenes.label: What changes for the PM
scenes.note: Managing quality through evaluation, not vibes.

scenes.at: The end state is a product org
scenes.label: The end state
scenes.text: Agents do the repetitive first-draft work. People do the judgment, collaboration and decisions.

scenes.at: Pick one workflow that repeats weekly
scenes.label: A plan you can run next week
items: Pick one workflow that repeats weekly
Define two agents for it, not four
Give each a clear output and cadence
Run a weekly review for two weeks
Refine based on what got used
itemAt: Give each agent a clear output

scenes.at: The goal is not to build the perfect AI product team
scenes.text: Build the first version that earns a permanent place in how your team operates.

scenes.at: This was Your First AI Product Team
